EX-99.1 2 d159635dex991.htm EX-99.1 EX-99.1 Exhibit 99.1 Rein Therapeutics Announces Preliminary Blinded Phase 2 RENEW Data Showing Encouraging Lung Function Trends in Patients with Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis and Reports Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results • 33% of evaluable patients demonstrated improvement over baseline in forced vital capacity (FVC) at Week 12 • From baseline, change in FVC ranged from an improvement of 338 ml to a decline of 349 ml at Week 12 • Low discontinuation rates, and favorable safety and tolerability observed across placebo and treatment groups, with no serious adverse events assessed as related to study treatment • Study has achieved 75% enrollment, with 90 patients randomized to date; on track to report topline data in 2027 AUSTIN, Texas, November 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ — Rein Therapeutics (“Rein”) (NASDAQ: RNTX), a biopharmaceutical company advancing a novel pipeline of first-in-class medicines in orphan pulmonary and fibrosis indications, today announced preliminary blinded twelve-week observations from the ongoing RENEW Phase 2 trial evaluating its lead drug candidate, LTI-03, in patients with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF).

We remain committed to advancing the study toward completion and look forward to reporting unblinded topline data in 2027.” Third Quarter 2026 and Recent Business Updates Clinical Updates The RENEW study is a randomized, placebo-controlled Phase 2 trial evaluating inhaled LTI-03 in patients with IPF.
• No serious adverse events related to study treatment have been reported as of the interim data cutoff.

• On track to report topline data in 2027: As of November, Rein has achieved 75% of the trial’s planned enrollment, with 90 out of approximately 120 patients randomized to date across the United States, United Kingdom, Australia, Germany and Poland.
Enrollment is tracking ahead of schedule and the Company remains on track to report topline data in 2027.
“Blinded interim data from our ongoing Phase 2 RENEW trial provides an early look at the safety, tolerability and lung function trends we are observing across the study population.
The Company expects the trial to remain blinded throughout enrollment and patient follow-up, and to report topline results in 2027.
